correctness.rationale: A complete eventwise proof checks precisely S=h-1 and S=h pivot events for the two unequal donor/proxy votes. Equality of central binomial coefficients yields a closed gain formula; division by the larger exponential base yields monotonicity of its two-state sign expression for every odd n. Both explicit reverse-direction rational examples and finite rational independent-convolution checks confirm computations; no finite experiment substitutes for the universal proof.

evidence: Gilbert et al. 2026 gives mechanisms under statewise dominance and asymptotic do-no-harm, not exact finite-size one-edge sign behavior.
Chatterjee et al. 2025 gives local mechanisms for graph families with variance requirements, not all-n signed advantage formulas.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem that an algorithm has an asymptotic concentration guarantee does not imply that a particular edge has an exact all-n gain formula or that the gain changes sign at most once. Neither broader paper supplies an all-n pointwise dominance theorem that covers the harmful-to-helpful and helpful-to-harmful examples.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The present statement implies a finite-size bound on the number of reversals across all odd populations and two constructive reversals under strict statewise recipient competence dominance. The inspected theorems do not entail this: their conclusions concern asymptotic global mechanisms, individual strategic utilities, or subjective factions. Abstract-only material for the 2026 two-faction study is not treated as a full-text exclusion.

evidence: Gilbert et al., arXiv:2608.16738, sections 2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4, 5: common-signal voting, mean-competence counterexamples, and concentration diagnostics; no one-edge population-phase identity located.
Bloembergen et al., arXiv:1802.08020, model/equilibrium and group-accuracy sections: no exact signal-mixture one-edge majority pivot criterion.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A logistic donor/proxy competence condition by itself covers a single signal state, not a two-state mixture. The combined theorem gives a sign law over all odd population sizes with possible reverse directions, and its proof depends on the precise two central binomial events. No inspected source had an equivalent statement or a direct stronger theorem.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The claim is an all-integer formula and phase classification, not an entry in an external lookup table. The inspected source figures have different delegations and probability vectors, so they cannot supply the stated formula by lookup.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of one-edge pivotal majority gain, size-varying implications, and mixed-signal sign changes against a full common-signal primary paper and several relevant delegation works found no implication of this exact claim. Related exact binomial and social-choice records concern different variables or rule families. The source comparison is qualified by an inaccessible full paper and unindexed-priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier exact pivotality or proxy-voting calculation may imply the same two-state classification.
The full PDF for the two-opposing-factions IACR preprint was inaccessible; its accessible abstract suggests different objectives but does not prove full-paper noncoverage.
Claim is strictly limited to a single edge and homogeneous background conditional on each signal.

value.rationale: A single competence-improving delegation is a natural atomic intervention. The formula exposes an exact safety condition involving the background electorate, and establishes a global one-crossing constraint across all odd population sizes. The two strictly competent examples exhibit both phase directions, showing the sharpness of the structural law without invoking unrelated asymptotic limits.
